text:
No, Victoria, do not take me, he answered. His whole soul flowed toward her and he wanted to say more, say more; it turned into confused outbursts, he was as though intoxicated. Yes, but Victoria, if you are a little fond of me .... I do not know, but say that you are, even if it is not so. Please. Oh, I should promise you to become something, become much, almost unheard-of much. You have no idea what I could become; I brood on it sometimes and know that I am utterly full of deeds not yet done. Many a time it streams out of me; at night I walk up and down, rocking, on the floor of my room because I am full of visions. There is a man in the room next door, he cannot sleep, he knocks on the wall. When morning dawns he comes in to me and is furious. It does not matter, I do not care about him; for by then I have thought of you for so long that I feel you are with me. I go to the window and sing, it is beginning to grow a little light, the poplars rustle outside. Good night! I say to the day. It is for you. Now she is asleep, I think, good night, God bless her! Then I lie down. Thus it goes evening after evening. But I have never believed that you were as lovely as you are. Now I shall remember you like this when you go away; as you are now. I shall remember you so clearly ....

Are you not coming home?

No. I am not finished. Yes, I am coming. I am leaving now. I am not finished, but I shall do all manner of things. Do you sometimes wander in the garden at home now? Do you ever go out in the evening? I could see you, I could perhaps be allowed to greet you, it is not for anything else. But if you are a little fond of me, if you can tolerate me, endure me, then say .... Do me that kindness .... Do you know, there is a palm that flowers only once in its life, and yet it grows to be seventy years old, the talipot palm. But it flowers only once. Now I am flowering. Yes, I shall get myself some money and travel home. I shall sell what I have written; I am, in fact, writing a large book, and I shall sell it now, first thing tomorrow, everything I have finished. I shall get quite a lot for it. Would you then want me to come home?

Yes.
Thank you, thank you! Forgive me if I hope too much, believe too much; it is so lovely to believe extraordinarily much. This is the happiest day I have lived ....

He took off his hat and laid it beside him.

Victoria looked around; a lady was coming down the street and, farther up, a woman with a basket. Victoria grew uneasy, she reached for her watch.

Must you go now? he asked. Say something before you go, let me hear your .... I love you and say it now. It will then depend on your answer whether I .... You have such absolute power over me. What is your answer?

A pause.

He lowers his head.
No, do not say it! he begged.

Not here, she answered. I shall do it down there.

They walked on.

They say that you are to marry the little girl, the girl, the one you rescued; what is her name?

Camilla, do you mean?

Camilla Seier. They say that you are to marry her.

Indeed. Why do you ask about that? She is not grown up. I have been in her home, it is so large and rich, a castle like your own; I have been there many times. No, she is not grown up.

She is fifteen years old. I have met her, we have spent time together. I became very taken with her. How charming she is!

I am not going to marry her, he said.

Oh, you are not.

He looked at her. A twitch passed over his face.

But why do you say this now? Do you wish to direct my attention to someone else?

She walked on with rapid steps and did not answer. They found themselves outside the chamberlain’s house. She took his hand and pulled him through the gateway, up the stairs.

I am not going inside, he said, half astonished.

She pressed the bell, turned toward him, and her breast heaved.

I love you, she said. Do you understand that? It is you I love.

Suddenly she pulled him quickly down the stairs again, three, four steps, flung her arms around him, and kissed him. She trembled against him.

It is you I love, she said.

The entrance door opened above. She tore herself free and hurried up the stairs.

IV

It is drawing toward morning, the day is dawning, a bluish, trembling September morning.

The poplars in the garden murmur softly. A window opens, a man leans out of it and hums. He has no coat on, he looks out into the world like an undressed madman who has drunk himself drunk on happiness during the night.

He suddenly turns away from the window and looks toward his door; someone has knocked. He calls: Come in! A man enters.

Good morning! he says to the man entering.
It is an elderly man, he is pale and furious, and he carries a lamp because it is not yet quite light.

Once again I must ask you to consider, Mr. Møller, Mr. Johannes Møller, whether you think this is reasonable, the man stammers bitterly.

No, Johannes answers, you are right. I have written something, it came to me so readily; look, I have written all this, I have been fortunate tonight. But now I am finished. I opened the window and sang a little.

You bellowed, says the man. It is the loudest singing I have heard, do you understand? And it is still the middle of the night.

Johannes seizes his papers on the table, takes a handful of large and small sheets.

Look here! he cries. I tell you, it has never gone so well for me. It was like a long flash of lightning. I once saw a flash of lightning that followed a telegraph wire, God help you, it looked like a sheet of fire. That is how it has streamed within me tonight. What am I to do? I do not think you will hold anything against me any longer when you hear how matters stand. I sat here and wrote, do you hear, I did not move; I remembered you and kept quiet. Then comes the moment when I no longer remember it, my breast was about to burst; perhaps I got up then, perhaps I also got up once more during the night and walked around the floor a few times. I was so happy.

I did not hear you very much tonight, says the man. But it is utterly unforgivable of you to open the window now at this time of day and bawl like that.

Very well. Yes, it is unforgivable. But now I have explained it to you. I have had a night without equal, you should know. Yesterday I experienced something. I am walking along the street and meet my happiness, oh, listen to me, meet my star and my happiness. Do you know, and then she kisses me. Her mouth was so red and I love her, she kisses me and intoxicates me. Have you ever trembled so violently in the mouth that you could not speak? I could not speak, my heart shook my whole body. I ran home and fell asleep; I sat here on the chair and slept. When evening came I awoke. My soul rocked up and down within me with emotion, and I began to write. What did I write? Here it is! I was possessed by a strange and glorious train of thought, the heavens opened, it was like a warm summer’s day for my soul, I received wine from an angel, I drank it; it was intoxicating wine, I drank it from a pomegranate bowl. Did I hear the clock strike? Did I see the lamp burn out? God grant that you understood it! I lived through it all anew, once again; I walked again with my beloved along the street and everyone turned to look after her. We walked in the park, we met the king, I swept my hat to the ground before him for joy, and the king turned to look after her, after my beloved, for she is so noble and lovely. We went down into the town again and all the schoolchildren turned to look after her, for she is young and wears a light-colored dress. When we came to a red stone house we went in. I followed her up the stairs and wanted to kneel before her. Then she put her arms around me and kissed me. This happened to me yesterday evening, it was no longer ago than that. If you asked me what I have written, then it is one single unceasing song to joy, to the happiness I have written. It was as though happiness lay naked before me with a long, laughing neck and desired me.
